summary: This bill bars any federal funds—including the Judgment Fund or victim compensation funds—from being used to pay compensation, restitution refunds, or similar awards to people prosecuted or convicted for the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack (even if later pardoned), and forbids creating any compensation fund for them.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly prohibits the use of any Federal funds (including the Judgment Fund and victim compensation funds) to compensate individuals prosecuted or convicted for January 6 involvement, and bars creation of any such compensation fund. It also redirects any already-paid fines/restitution to the Architect of the Capitol rather than refunding them. This is a direct restriction on federal expenditures, pushing toward reduced government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy or funding.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, borders, or related pathways.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food stamps, or similar safety-net spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to education funding or policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.

The bill addresses individuals already prosecuted or convicted for January 6 offenses by denying them compensation or refunds of fines/restitution. While this reinforces the financial consequences of those convictions, it does not alter sentencing, policing practices, rehabilitation programs, or broader criminal-justice reform. The connection is therefore tangential at best.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.

By prohibiting specific uses of federal funds and redirecting collected fines to the Architect of the Capitol, the bill reduces potential outlays from the Treasury. This has a minor, indirect effect of supporting debt-reduction priorities rather than accepting additional deficit spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill contains no provisions related to labor, unions, or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
